title: Uterine-fibroid symptom severity check-in (UFS-QoL Symptom Severity)
description: The 8-item Symptom Severity subscale of the Uterine Fibroid Symptom and Health-Related Quality of Life Questionnaire (UFS-QoL). The full UFS-QoL also includes a 29-item HRQL subscale; this is the validated short form clinicians use to track fibroid-related bleeding, pressure, and bulk-symptom severity over time. Used at baseline and at 3-month follow-up for patients with confirmed or suspected fibroids.

items.text: In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by heavy bleeding during your menstrual period?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by passing blood clots during your menstrual period?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by the irregular or unpredictable timing of your periods?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by the length (number of days) of your menstrual period?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by feeling tightness or pressure in your pelvic area?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by frequent urination during the daytime hours?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by getting up at night to urinate?
In the past 3 months, how distressed were you by feeling fatigued or worn out from fibroid-related symptoms?

scoring.note: Sum the eight item values (range 8–40). Transform to 0–100: (raw − 8) × 100 / 32. Higher = more severe symptoms.

interpretation_bands.label: minimal
interpretation_bands.patient_label: Fibroid-related symptoms are minimal right now.

interpretation_bands.label: substantial
interpretation_bands.patient_label: Fibroid-related symptoms are substantially affecting your daily life.

interpretation_bands.label: severe
interpretation_bands.patient_label: Fibroid-related symptoms are severely affecting your quality of life.

thresholds.message: UFS-QoL Symptom Severity ≥50 — fibroid symptoms substantially affecting life. Consider escalating to definitive management discussion.
UFS-QoL Symptom Severity ≥75 — severe symptom burden. Same-week visit or escalation recommended.
UFS-QoL has worsened by ≥25 points compared to baseline. Earlier follow-up advisable.

citation: Spies JB, Coyne K, Guaou N, Boyle D, Skyrnarz-Murphy K, Gonzalves SM. The UFS-QOL, a new disease-specific symptom and health-related quality of life questionnaire for leiomyomata. Obstet Gynecol 2002;99(2):290-300. PMID: 11814511
